question: A victim of an acid attack has bright yellow staining of skin and mucosae at contact sites. Which acid is most likely responsible?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Nitric acid causes the xanthoproteic reaction — it nitrates aromatic amino acids in skin proteins, producing characteristic bright yellow colour (xanthos = yellow in Greek). This is a pathognomonic forensic identifier for nitric acid contact.
Incorrect. Sulphuric acid causes black-brown burns due to dehydration and carbonisation of organic tissue (charring). It does not produce yellow staining.
Incorrect. Hydrochloric acid causes pale white-to-grey burns with a pungent smell. There is no yellow discolouration with HCl contact.

Incorrect. Carbolic acid (phenol) produces white-then-brown burns with a characteristic phenolic odour and local anaesthetic effect (the patient may feel little pain despite severe injury). It does not cause yellow staining.

overallFeedback.feedback: The correct answer is nitric acid. The xanthoproteic reaction (yellow skin staining from protein nitration) is pathognomonic of nitric acid. Colour key: H₂SO₄ = black-brown; HCl = pale white; carbolic = white-brown with anaesthesia.
Correct. Acid identification by wound colour: nitric acid = yellow (xanthoproteic); sulphuric acid = black-brown (charring); HCl = pale white-grey; carbolic acid = white-then-brown with anaesthesia.
